sections.PDD Edit section 1.1: This document describes how "Vendor invoice processing (India, company code 1000)" is done today, step by step, and how it will be done once automated. It is the reference for the requirements (FRD) and the solution design (SDD).
sections.PDD Edit section 1.2: Pay suppliers accurately and on time; reduce receipt-to-posting cycle time, meet the MSE 45-day payment rule and capture early payment discounts.
sections.PDD Edit section 1.4:
• Access to SAP S/4HANA for the automation (Screens: 1 confirmed, 1 not available. API: 5 not available).

  • Access to AP shared mailbox (Microsoft 365) for the automation (API: confirmed).

  • Access to SharePoint library "AP Invoices" for the automation (API: confirmed).

  • Access to AP tracker (Excel on SharePoint) for the automation (File: reported, not confirmed).

  • Access to Office scanner (Pune) for the automation (Not provided).
sections.PDD Edit section 3.2: RPA-led automation. Of 20 steps people do today: Rule-based RPA for 15, AI-assisted automation for 1, 4 stay with people. 1 step is already done by a system.
sections.PDD Edit section 3.5:
• Outside the process: Payment run (F110), performed by Treasury

  • Outside the process: Vendor master creation and changes

  • Outside the process: Employee expense claims (SAP Concur)

  • Outside the process: Kaveri UK Ltd. on Workday Financials

  • Outside the process: Month-end GR/IR clearing, accruals and GST input credit reconciliation (GSTR-2B)

  • Outside the process: Vendor credit notes (deferred to a separate session)

  • Outside the process: Vendor payment status queries
sections.SDD Edit section 1: The solution for Vendor invoice processing (India, company code 1000) has 6 automation units covering 16 of 21 steps. The remaining steps stay with people, as set out in the PDD section "Delivery model". What each unit must do is in the FRD.
sections.SDD Edit section 11: Proposed, not confirmed: each automation unit is tested on its own first, then end to end with the applications, then by the business against the scenarios above. Every exception path above has at least one scenario.
sections.BRD Edit section 1:
Recommended for Vendor invoice processing (India, company code 1000): RPA-led automation. Rule-based RPA is the best fit for 15 of the 16 steps open to automation, mainly because no judgment is needed and the input is structured data.

  • Of 20 steps people do today: Rule-based RPA for 15, AI-assisted automation for 1, 4 stay with people. 1 step is already done by a system.

  • Readiness: Ready to automate. No major change is expected, and the rules are stable enough to build on.

  • Up to 20,900 hands-on hours a year could be automated.

  • Priority is not settled yet. The value could lie on either side of 1,000 hours a year. The build effort depends on facts not yet known.
sections.BRD Edit section 2: Pay suppliers accurately and on time; reduce receipt-to-posting cycle time, meet the MSE 45-day payment rule and capture early payment discounts.
sections.BRD Edit section 6: Today the process has 21 steps carried out by 8 roles across 7 applications. It handles 9,500 cases/month. The step-by-step detail is in the PDD section "Detailed As-Is steps".
sections.BRD Edit section 7: What the solution must do to meet them is in the FRD, with a traceability matrix.
sections.FRD Edit section 1: This document states what the solution for Vendor invoice processing (India, company code 1000) must do, as requirements that can each be tested. Why the change is made is in the BRD; how the work is done today is in the PDD section "Detailed As-Is steps".
sections.FRD Edit section 3.1: The solution shall log invoice in AP shared mailbox (Microsoft 365), SharePoint library "AP Invoices" and AP tracker (Excel on SharePoint).
sections.FRD Edit section 3.2: The solution shall pass "Log invoice" to AP Clerk to review before the case continues.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.4: The solution shall validate vendor in SAP S/4HANA.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.5: The solution shall return invoice to vendor in AP shared mailbox (Microsoft 365) and AP tracker (Excel on SharePoint).
sections.FRD Edit section 3.6: The solution shall check for duplicates in SAP S/4HANA and AP tracker (Excel on SharePoint).
sections.FRD Edit section 3.7: The solution shall raise vendor master request in ServiceNow and AP tracker (Excel on SharePoint).
sections.FRD Edit section 3.8: The solution shall enter PO invoice in SAP S/4HANA.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.9: The solution shall request non-PO approval in AP shared mailbox (Microsoft 365).
sections.FRD Edit section 3.10: The solution shall pass "Approve non-PO invoice" to Cost Centre Owner / DoA approver to decide on before the case continues.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.11: The solution shall park invoice and request goods receipt in SAP S/4HANA, AP shared mailbox (Microsoft 365) and AP tracker (Excel on SharePoint).
sections.FRD Edit section 3.12: The solution shall post goods receipt in SAP S/4HANA.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.13: The solution shall enter non-PO invoice in SAP S/4HANA and SharePoint library "AP Invoices".
sections.FRD Edit section 3.14: The solution shall park invoice and refer variance in SAP S/4HANA, AP shared mailbox (Microsoft 365) and AP tracker (Excel on SharePoint).
sections.FRD Edit section 3.15: The solution shall post invoice and attach PDF in SAP S/4HANA.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.16: The solution shall pass "Review high-value invoice" to AP Team Lead to decide on before the case continues.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.17: The solution shall pass "Investigate variance" to Buyer (Procurement) to decide on before the case continues.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.18: The solution shall update tracker to Posted in AP tracker (Excel on SharePoint).
sections.FRD Edit section 3.19: The solution shall amend purchase order in SAP S/4HANA.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.20: The solution shall request credit note or revised invoice in AP shared mailbox (Microsoft 365).
sections.FRD Edit section 3.21: When a mandatory field is missing or wrong, the solution shall apply the stated handling: return to vendor using template AP-T01; and route the case to the Vendor.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.22: When invoice addressed to another entity, e.g. the UK company, the solution shall apply the stated handling: return to vendor; and route the case to the Vendor.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.23: When vendor or Kaveri GSTIN on the invoice does not match, the solution shall apply the stated handling: return to vendor for a corrected invoice; and route the case to the Vendor.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.24: When bank details on invoice differ from SAP vendor master, the solution shall apply the stated handling: hold; ServiceNow request to Vendor Master Data; call-back verification; and route the case to the Vendor Master Data team.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.25: When same vendor, invoice number and gross amount already recorded, the solution shall apply the stated handling: do not post; confirm with vendor; mark duplicate; and route the case to the AP Clerk.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.26: When no GR exists for the invoiced quantity, the solution shall apply the stated handling: park; request GR; remind at 3, escalate at 7 working days; and route the case to the Requester / Stores.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.27: When invoice price exceeds PO price beyond tolerance, the solution shall apply the stated handling: park; refer to buyer; and route the case to the Buyer (Procurement).
sections.FRD Edit section 3.28: When invoiced quantity is more than the GR quantity, the solution shall apply the stated handling: park and ask stores for the difference; and route the case to the Requester / Stores.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.29: When no reply from approver, the solution shall apply the stated handling: remind at 2 and escalate at 5 working days; and route the case to the Finance Controller.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.30: When PDF cannot be opened, the solution shall apply the stated handling: request a readable copy from the vendor; and route the case to the Vendor.
sections.FRD Edit section 3.31: When MIRO reports the PO is being edited by the buyer in ME22N, the solution shall apply the stated handling: wait and retry later; and route the case to the AP Clerk.
sections.FRD Edit section 5: Interfaces that are unknown or only reported are not assumed to work; their status is an open item until someone accountable confirms it.
sections.Agent Edit section 1: This document sets out what AI would do in "Vendor invoice processing (India, company code 1000)": the 1 of 21 step rated AI-assisted in the assessment, where it reads or drafts and a person checks the result. No step is agentic, so nothing here acts on its own; "the agent" below means this AI assistance. It also sets out where a person stays, what the AI may use, and how its work is checked. The process as a whole is in the PDD; how the solution is built is in the SDD.
sections.Agent Edit section 3: The other steps, and who or what does them, so the hand-overs to and from the agent are clear.
sections.Agent Edit section 9: Proposed, not confirmed: the agent is first tried on past cases whose right outcome is known, then run beside people (people decide; the agent's answer is compared), and works on its own only once the agreed share of right outcomes is reached.
